title: Data classification scheme and schema-level assignment
status_rationale: UNB-TEC-003 and SOC2-014 require explicit classification; UNB-TEN-007 defines a four-way classification for shared services; UNB-API-STD-001 requires a privacy classification per API. No scheme has been adopted.
target_answer: Unbound uses a four-level scheme (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) plus orthogonal tags for tenant scope and regulated categories (financial account, government identifier, donor anonymity, sanctions screening). Every column, event field, document type, log field, API field and AI prompt template is classified in its definition; the build fails on unclassified elements; derived data inherits the highest classification of its inputs unless a reviewed declassification rule applies.
current_practice: Not established. No scheme adopted; classification exists only as requirement text.
intended_practice: Adopt the scheme in the first data model; implement classification as schema metadata with a build gate.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify explicit classification of personal and financial data and of every API field. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
owner: Data governance owner (proposed role; not appointed)
open_questions: Does Strata support arbitrary column metadata for classification tags, and can the F# domain model carry classification at the type level?

title: Labeling and handling rules by classification, including AI agents and egress
status_rationale: UNB-PLAT-003 requires Folio for generated documents; UNB-DOC-004 requires role-scoped delivery and controlled redaction; SOC2-003 restricts sensitive data in logs. No handling standard exists.
target_answer: Each classification has a handling standard covering storage encryption, transmission, display masking, export, printing, email and retention. Folio-rendered documents and exports carry visible classification labels and embedded metadata. Restricted data cannot be sent by email or placed in tickets; outbound channels carry tokens or secure links instead. AI agent tools declare which classifications they may read and return, and the tool gateway refuses calls that would exceed them.
intended_practice: Write the handling standard; implement labels in Folio templates and classification-aware tool permissions.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify role-scoped, redacted document delivery and privacy-aware logging. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
owner: Data governance owner (proposed role; not appointed)
open_questions: Can Folio embed classification metadata in generated PDFs, and does it support visible labels in templates? Folio capability is unverified (UNB-PLAT-003).

title: Restricted data: bank account numbers, SSNs and TINs, government identifiers
status_rationale: SEC-CRYPTO-001 requires managed keys; UNB-TEC-003 requires explicit policies for personal and financial data; UNB-DATA-007 keeps unnecessary PII out of immutable payloads. Nacha data security rules require account numbers to be unreadable at rest for parties above volume thresholds. No restricted-data design exists.
target_answer: Bank account and routing numbers, SSNs, TINs and government ID numbers are stored only in a tokenization vault with field-level encryption under separately managed keys; application records and events hold tokens. Displays show masked values by default; unmasking requires a declared purpose, role and step-up authentication and is logged. SSN or TIN is collected only where a documented need exists (for example identity proofing or tax reporting) and is never written to logs, events, exports or prompts. Nacha's unreadable-at-rest expectation is met regardless of volume threshold.
intended_practice: Design the tokenization vault together with the identity vault (UNB-DATA-007); define the collection-need register.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify explicit classification and protection of financial records and personal information with managed keys. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
owner: Data governance owner (proposed role; not appointed)
open_questions: Does Unbound, as a Nacha third-party service provider (CNV-PAY-001), meet the volume threshold that makes the Nacha account-number rule binding, or is it adopted voluntarily?

history.change: BL-021: set institutional_acceptance to unknown (prior 'likely' was unsourced agent judgment, kept in supporting_arguments) and added an unvalidated-acceptance note to opposing_arguments (OBJ-VRM-019, OBJ-SKEPTIC-014).

challenge.customer_intent: Customer wants bank and tax identifiers protected beyond ordinary database encryption.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Mass theft of account numbers and SSNs leading to fraud, identity theft and breach notification.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Volume or disk encryption protects only against media theft; anyone with application or database access reads plaintext.
challenge.legally_required: State breach laws treat these elements as triggering notification; Nacha rules require unreadable storage for covered parties above thresholds; no general statute mandates tokenization.
challenge.contractually_required: Bank customers commonly require field-level protection.
challenge.historical_convention: PCI DSS normalized tokenization for card data; similar practice is spreading to bank account data.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not collecting SSN at all where not needed eliminates the risk for that element.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Tokens in all application paths mean plaintext is reachable only through the vault interface.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Vault access logs and unmask events are continuous evidence.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Do-not-collect by default plus tokenization of whatever must be collected.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by schema inspection and vault access logs.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any path that copies plaintext out of the vault (exports, support, logs) defeats the design.
challenge.alternative_cost: Medium to high: vault and token plumbing.
challenge.alternative_risks: Vault availability becomes critical to payments.
supporting_arguments: Shrinks breach impact to the vault.
Clear evidence trail for every unmask.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Operational complexity and latency on payment paths.
Not eliminating collection where the sponsor insists on it.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Donor anonymity and disclosure preferences
status_rationale: ADM-013 requires public and private names, anonymity preferences and controlled disclosures. No design for enforcement through grant letters, payment remittance and charity portals exists.
target_answer: Each grant carries an effective disclosure preference (full name, fund name only, anonymous) set by the advisor within sponsor policy. Every outbound channel that mentions a donor (grant letters, check stubs, ACH remittance addenda, networked grant-platform payloads, charity portal views, acknowledgments) renders donor identity only through one disclosure function that applies the preference; the type system prevents raw donor names reaching outbound templates. Overrides require sponsor authority and are logged. Preferences survive migration and succession.
intended_practice: Model disclosure preference as a typed value that outbound templates must consume.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.

title: Data minimization in collection, storage and onward disclosure
status_rationale: UNB-DATA-007 directs avoiding unnecessary PII in immutable payloads; MON-014 and AIN-023 call for minimum necessary data; UNB-GAP-021 calls for minimization rules. No collection register exists.
target_answer: Every collected field is justified in a collection-need register linked to the schema; fields without a recorded purpose fail the build. Onward disclosures to subprocessors (identity proofing, sanctions screening, payment) send only fields the integration contract declares. Minimization is reviewed annually against actual field usage telemetry, and unused fields are retired.
intended_practice: Create the collection-need register as part of schema metadata.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text in the Unbound baseline (unbound@9b38de47) can be shown, and it proves intent, not operation.
customer_statement: Unbound is not yet in production. Its requirements specify keeping unnecessary personal data out of immutable records and using minimum necessary data in communications. This is a design commitment, not an operating control, and has not been independently verified.
external_assurance: None. No SOC 2 report, ISO certification, privacy assessment or other independent assurance exists for any Echelon service as of 2026-11-25.
